ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The main body in the figure is a transition-state structure. After ignoring the curved arrows, a benzene ring with an ortho OH is visible on the left; this aromatic ring is connected to an alkene carbon, and this alkene carbon is also connected to negatively charged O−. The other end of the alkene is connected to the benzylic carbon on the right, and this carbon is also connected to a benzene ring and is connected downward to a hydroperoxy fragment OOH. Then reason: According to the specified method, start from the hydroperoxide end and write OOC; the carbon after OOC is the benzylic carbon connecting the benzene ring and the alkene chain, so add a phenyl branch c1ccccc1; the alkene branch is written according to the depicted geometry and substituents as /C=C(\[O-])c1ccccc1O. Combining gives OOC(/C=C(\[O-])c1ccccc1O)c1ccccc1.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image? Ignore the arrows.

method.method_draft: Start the SMILES at the hydroperoxide end as OOC. Treat the carbon after OOC as the benzylic carbon bonded to a phenyl ring and to the alkene chain. Add the phenyl branch as c1ccccc1. For the alkene branch, encode the drawn geometry and substituents as /C=C(\[O-])c1ccccc1O, where the terminal alkene carbon bears the O− and the ortho-hydroxyphenyl group. Combine these pieces to obtain OOC(/C=C(\[O-])c1ccccc1O)c1ccccc1.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中主体是一个过渡态结构，忽略弯箭头后，可见左侧为带邻位 OH 的苯环；该芳环连接到一个烯烃碳，该烯烃碳还连有带负电的 O−。烯烃另一端连接到右侧的苄位碳，该碳同时连有一个苯环，并向下连接到过氧羟基片段 OOH。再推理：按指定方法从 hydroperoxide 端开始写作 OOC；OOC 后的碳是连接苯环和烯烃链的苄位碳，因此加苯基分支 c1ccccc1；烯烃分支按图示几何与取代基写为 /C=C(\[O-])c1ccccc1O。组合得到 OOC(/C=C(\[O-])c1ccccc1O)c1ccccc1。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct visual graph transcription: read the molecule as an atom-bond graph and then serialize it into SMILES. This is the natural single route for this image-to-SMILES task.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the drawing while ignoring all curved arrows. Identify two benzene rings, with the left ring bearing an ortho phenolic OH and attached to an enolate/vinylic carbon bearing O−. Read the central alkene connection to a benzylic carbon that is also bonded to a plain phenyl ring and to a hydroperoxy group OOH.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know the requested output is a SMILES expression and that the curved arrows in the transition-state drawing should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES syntax rules: aromatic phenyl rings as c1ccccc1, ortho phenol as c1ccccc1O when attached at the adjacent ring atom, negatively charged oxygen as [O-], hydroperoxide as OO, branches with parentheses, and slash/backslash notation to preserve the shown alkene geometry.
